jobs.title: Senior Product Manager
jobs.description: About us At Pencil, we are driving innovation in advertising technology through our state-of-the-art SaaS product, which harnesses Agentic AI to redefine content creation. Our mission is to make AI the default in advertising without replacing creative people. To achieve this, we need to make sure that our technology isn't just in the hands of big brands - we need to try to help small businesses and creative individuals too. The role Workflows are how most of the creative on Pencil gets made. A workflow is a visual sequence of steps, covering inputs, generation, brand assets, scoring, branching logic and delivery, that a person builds once and runs again whenever the job repeats, on demand or on a schedule. This role owns that product and the connections that feed it, with one goal: more workflows built and run, by more people, across every customer. You will own Workflows and Integrations. That covers the workflow builder, templates, scheduling and run management, and the steps that workflows are built from. It also covers the platform's third-party connections outside media: digital asset management systems, file storage such as Google Drive, translation services, data services such as Foreplay, and more than a hundred other business tools. You will make those connections part of the workflow itself, so that a run can start from a client's systems and deliver back into them. You will build them on a common framework, so that each new connection is quicker to ship than the last and client teams can build on it for individual clients. You will also own how workflows show up inside Scribble, our creative agent. Agents can already run as steps inside a workflow. The next step is for Scribble to find, build, change and run workflows on a person's behalf and report back as they run, and for a workflow to pause for a person's decision and act on it. You will work closely with the team that builds Scribble, and you will own the workflow experience it works through, so that a workflow behaves the same whether a person or an agent is driving it. When that works, building a workflow stops being a specialist job. Key responsibilities Own the charter for Workflows and Integrations: the durable problem, success metrics, and an explicit in and out scope list. Grow adoption across every customer, measured by the number of workflows built and run and the number of people building them. Make building a workflow simple enough for a marketer or creative to do without help, through templates, guided set-up and defaults that cover the common jobs. Own the workflow experience that Scribble works through, so that an agent can find, build, change and run a workflow with the same tools a person uses. Make human review part of the run: a workflow should pause for a person's decision, record it, and continue down the right path. Make runs dependable at volume, with scheduling, run management, failure handling and clear status, so that a team trusts a workflow to run unattended. Own third-party integrations outside media, from digital asset management and file storage to translation and data services, and make them built-in steps in a workflow, so that a run can start from a client's systems and deliver back into them. Set the integration framework and standards that client teams build on when they connect a system for a single client. Work with customers to find the jobs they repeat every week and turn them into workflows and templates that others can reuse. Run the full lifecycle from discovery to post-launch review, with a written hypothesis before every ship and a review against it afterwards. Use product data and structured customer feedback to set priorities, working backwards from evidenced customer need. Partner closely with design on the builder experience, and with engineering on run reliability and the integration framework. jobs.description: Software Engineer, Infrastructure Hybrid in Palo Alto (Mon / Wed / Thurs) Â· $185Kâ$215K base + meaningful early-stage equity + full benefits Â About Sodalis Specialty pharmacy is where the most complex and expensive drugs reach the most in-need patients, and it still runs on faxes, phone tag, and manual data entry. Patients wait weeks for therapies that can't wait. Sodalis is building AI agents that run those operations end to end: reading and validating prescriptions, handling phone calls, and moving prescriptions through eligibility and fulfillment. The ambition goes beyond that. We want to be the rails every specialty prescription runs on, and the first system to perform clinical review at the standard of a pharmacist. We're already in production, processing tens of thousands of prescriptions a week. Backed by Gradient Ventures (Google's AI fund), and founded by veterans of Apple's Applied ML, Included Health, and Avella Specialty Pharmacy (scaled to $1.5B+ before its acquisition by OptumRx). Â The Opportunity Everything we run today is cloud-based, and so are the pharmacy management systems we integrate with. But most of the specialty pharmacy market runs on-prem. To reach it, our system has to run on the pharmacy's systems instead of ours. Whether that's the full stack on-site or a hybrid split with our cloud is one of the first decisions you'd make. That's the problem you'd own. We've never shipped an on-prem deployment, so there's no pattern to follow. You'll decide how our architecture gets packaged and deployed into environments we don't control, what has to change in our current infrastructure to make that possible, and how we maintain and see into those deployments once they're live. We don't yet know what these environments look like in detail. Some pharmacies may have restricted outbound access, legacy hardware, or IT teams that can't give us a login; others may be more open. Part of the job is going in with our customer, finding out what's actually there, and designing something that works across the range. You'll start with our AI pharmacy tech product, rolling out with a committed customer, so you build against a real deployment instead of a hypothetical one. You'd work directly with the founders and the early engineering team on the architecture. What you'll do Decide how our architecture runs in a pharmacy's environment, starting with the AI pharmacy tech product: full stack on-site, a hybrid split with our cloud, or something in between. Adapt our current infrastructure and build the packaging and deployment path that installs and updates Sodalis at each pharmacy. Own those deployments over time: upgrades, rollbacks, and observability into health and failures without being on site. Go in with our customer and pharmacy IT teams to learn what their environments actually allow, and design for the range. Partner with the founders and early engineering team on architecture. What we're looking for 5+ years in infrastructure or platform engineering. You've taken an AWS-native stack and made it run on Kubernetes or similar in environments you don't operate, including stateful services. You've shipped and maintained software running in environments you don't control: on-prem, customer-hosted, edge, or embedded. You've kept a fleet of remote installs updated, observable, and recoverable without being able to log into them. You've set the first pattern for something in a startup and are comfortable with ambiguity. You'll spend time with pharmacy IT teams and need to understand their constraints firsthand. No healthcare background required. How we work We're a handful of people going all in on a problem we think is worth it, holding a high bar and shipping work that reaches real patients. It's intense, and it isn't for everyone. We want people who want to build something that matters, alongside others who care as much as they do. If that's you, we should talk. jobs.title: Rust Software Engineer - Rust / C++ (m/f/d)
jobs.description: Quantum Systems develops autonomous, multi-domain systems that operate in the air, on the ground and on the water. Behind every platform is software that has to work reliably in the real world, with limited resources, unreliable connectivity and no second chances. We are looking for software engineers who like to build exactly that kind of software in Rust and C++. You will join our engineering organization and work on production code that runs on real vehicles and sensors, across a broad range of challenges from low-level systems to scalable services. We are looking for engineers who quickly understand a complex system and its domain, and who use that understanding to get leverage: designing the architecture, setting the guardrails and guiding several AI agents at once to build, test and iterate faster, while taking full responsibility for the result. What is your Day to Day Mission: Build and maintain production-grade software in Rust and C++ for autonomous platforms and the systems around them. Design performant, fault-tolerant components that run on embedded Linux, edge hardware and in the cloud. Develop communication layers, data pipelines and real-time processing for sensor-driven, distributed systems. Work with hardware and robotics engineers to get software from simulation and test benches onto real vehicles. Use AI agents as part of your daily engineering workflow: break down problems, run several agents in parallel, review their output critically and make sure it meets our quality and safety standards. Own your code end to end: design, review, testing, deployment and troubleshooting of systems in the field. Shape architecture decisions and help raise engineering standards in a growing team. What you bring to the team: Several years of professional experience (ideally 4+) building software in Rust and/or C++, including production code. A strong foundation in systems programming: concurrency, memory and resource management, networking and performance tuning. The ability to understand a complex system and its domain quickly, and to translate that understanding into clear architecture and well-scoped tasks. Hands-on experience working with AI coding agents, or the curiosity and drive to build that skill fast, including the judgment to verify and correct what they produce. Day-to-day experience with Linux as a development and target environment. Experience with distributed, real-time or performance-critical systems. A solid testing mindset, from unit tests to hardware-in-the-loop or simulation. Clear communication and the ability to work independently in a fast-moving, interdisciplinary environment. Nice to have Experience with robotics, autonomy or sensor integration. Experience setting up agent-based workflows, such as parallel agents, automated test and review loops or custom tooling around coding agents. Embedded or real-time experience (RTOS, bare metal, firmware). Familiarity with ROS 2 or simulation frameworks. Knowledge of communication protocols and low-latency data transport. Experience with containers, CI/CD and cloud infrastructure. Our benefits: Company pension scheme: We support you so that you can already make provisions for later. Flexible working hours: With trust-based working hours, you are not only responsible for your working hours, but also for your work-life balance. Bei uns bekommst du qualifizierte Termine mit Entscheidern und konzentrierst dich auf das, was du am besten kannst: abschließen. FAKTOR MENSCH ist ein Hamburger Spezialist für betriebliche Krankenversicherung (bKV). Wir begleiten mittelständische Unternehmen von der Beratung über das Onboarding bis zur laufenden Administration. Arbeitgeber binden damit Fachkräfte, senken Fehlzeiten und bieten einen Benefit, der wirklich genutzt wird. jobs.title: Vertrieb Industriewasseraufbereitung (m/w/d)
jobs.description: Unser Kunde ist ein etabliertes und wachstumsstarkes Unternehmen in der Umweltbranche mit den Geschäftsbereichen Industriewassermanagement und Entsorgung & Verwertung. Als führender Anbieter für Betriebsführungs- und Betreiberlösungen in der industriellen Abwasseraufbereitung und Prozesswasserbehandlung bietet das Unternehmen ein breites Portfolio für das Wassermanagement in der produzierenden Industrie – von Betriebsführungskonzepten über Wartung und Instandhaltung bis hin zu eigenen Betriebschemikalien. Wir suchen keine Verwalter – wir suchen echte Macher mit Vertriebsgen. Menschen, die Chancen erkennen, Verantwortung übernehmen und den Anspruch haben, beim Kunden wirklich etwas zu bewegen. Das Unternehmen ist Teil einer international aufgestellten, vertikal integrierten Unternehmensgruppe mit rund 45 Gesellschaften und entsprechendem Zugang zu Infrastruktur, Technologie und Verwertungswegen sowie echten Wettbewerbsvorteilen im Markt. Am Standort München oder in der Filiale in Offenbach an der Queich arbeitest du nah am Markt und übernimmst eine aktive Rolle im Ausbau des Geschäfts. Du bist nicht nur Ansprechpartner, sondern Treiber: Du erkennst Potenziale, entwickelst Lösungen und bringst sie beim Kunden auf die Straße. Dabei kannst du dich auf ein erfahrenes Team im Hintergrund verlassen, das dich operativ unterstützt. Aufgaben Du gewinnst neue Industrie- und Gewerbekunden für unsere Lösungen im Bereich Industriewasser, Abwasserbehandlung und Entsorgung und betreust den bestehenden Kundenstamm; dabei berätst du zu wasserwirtschaftlichen und abfalltechnischen Fragestellungen. Du analysierst Kundenprozesse (z. B. Prozesswasser, Abwasserströme), bewertest Stoffströme und entwickelst passende Lösungen – von der Aufbereitung über Kreislaufführung bis zur Entsorgung. Du erstellst Kalkulationen sowie Angebote und bringst technische Lösungen wirtschaftlich sauber auf den Punkt; Markt- und Wettbewerbsanalysen gehören ebenfalls zu deinem Aufgabengebiet. Du verhandelst eigenverantwortlich Verträge, führst Preis- und Vertragsverhandlungen und schließt Verträge mit Neu- und Bestandskunden ab. Du begleitest Projekte und Großaufträge, koordinierst interne Schnittstellen (Technik, Betrieb, Logistik) und stellst eine reibungslose Umsetzung sicher. Du pflegst Kundendaten und Dokumentationen und stellst sicher, dass alle abfall- und wasserrechtlichen Vorschriften sowie Qualitätsrichtlinien eingehalten werden. Du beobachtest den Markt, erkennst Trends im Bereich Industriewasser und Kreislaufwirtschaft und repräsentierst das Unternehmen auf Fachmessen. Qualifikation Erfolgreich abgeschlossenes Studium oder Ausbildung in der Abfall-/Wasserwirtschaft, Verfahrenstechnik, Umwelttechnik, Chemie beziehungsweise eine vergleichbare kaufmännische oder technische Qualifikation. Erfahrung im Vertrieb von Entsorgungs-, Umwelt- oder wassertechnischen Dienstleistungen sowie in der Projektbegleitung; idealerweise auch Erfahrung in der Wasser- und Abwassertechnik oder der industriellen Prozesswasserbehandlung. Fundiertes Verständnis der Abfallwirtschaft, Kreislaufwirtschaft sowie grundlegender wasserwirtschaftlicher Prozesse; Fähigkeit, Stoffströme und Prozesszusammenhänge zu bewerten. Ausgeprägtes Kommunikations-, Verhandlungs- und Präsentationsgeschick. Selbstständige, strukturierte Arbeitsweise, Teamfähigkeit und sicherer Umgang mit MS-Office-Anwendungen. Erfahrung mit der Bestimmung der Trockensubstanzkonzentration (CTS) und Umgang mit entsprechenden Analyseverfahren ist ein Plus. Sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse und umgangssprachliche Englischkenntnisse. Führerschein der Klasse B und Reisebereitschaft. Benefits Sicherer Arbeitsplatz in einer nachhaltigen Zukunftsbranche mit langfristiger Perspektive. Transparente Vergütung mit erfolgsabhängiger Leistungsvergütung, Spesen und Corporate Benefits. Dienstwagen zur privaten Nutzung inklusive Tankkarte. Flexible Arbeitsmodelle mit Home‑Office‑Möglichkeit und familienfreundlichen Arbeitszeiten. Intensive Einarbeitun

jobs.title: Product Manager - Snacks
jobs.description: Vilgain makes high-quality food - clean, functional ingredients, no shortcuts, no filler additives . We're 700+ people across Prague, Brno and London, already selling in 12+ markets across Europe, the UK, the US and beyond. We're on a mission to change how people think about food , and we're growing fast to do it - expanding internationally and building a company where people have a real say in what we make and how we make it, not just a seat at the table. Your mission 🎯 You'll own specific product development projects from brief to launch, working directly with third-party suppliers and manufacturers. Working closely with the Category Manager, you'll make sure every project is aligned with the wider category goals and launch plan, and spot the commercial opportunities that will help the category grow. What will you do? Owning end-to-end new product development projects, from initial brief through development to market launch. Running projects with third-party manufacturers – sourcing and selecting suppliers and managing those relationships day to day. Reporting into the Category Manager and making sure your projects are aligned with the wider category goals and launch plan. Building the commercial case for your projects – costings, margins and volumes – and prioritising the opportunities with the highest value. Partnering with design, marketing, Regulatory and QA to bring products to market, including briefs, documentation and artwork sign-off. Running existing product development (EPD) projects such as product improvements, packaging amends and label corrections. Monitoring market trends and identifying new commercial opportunities for the category. What do we expect from you? At least 3 years' experience in NPD, project management or a similar role in the food industry – food experience is essential. Experience with private label production and working with third-party manufacturers. Highly numerate and financially aware, with the commercial sense to prioritise high-value opportunities. Experience in a small business or startup environment – we move quickly, and you'll need to be happy with the fast pace of a rapidly growing business. Highly organised, with strong attention to detail and the ability to juggle several projects at once. A proactive problem-solver who takes initiative and can work independently. A strong communicator who can build good relationships with colleagues, both internally and externally. Confident with spreadsheets and project management tools, and actively uses AI tools to work smarter. A love for food and a genuine interest in making a difference to the food system. Fluent in English. What we offer: Based in London, hybrid – minimum 3 days a week in the office. Fast-paced, growing team where your work has a visible impact on the products we launch. 5 weeks of vacation, flexible hours, and remote work options, get monthly shopping credits. Stay connected through team events, breakfasts, and group workouts. Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

jobs.title: Senior Pricing Analyst, B2B
jobs.description: Relay is fundamentally reshaping how goods move in an online era. Backed by Europe’s largest-ever logistics Series A ($35M) led by deep-tech investors Plural, and a recently closed Series B ($95M), Relay is scaling faster than 99% of venture-backed startups. We're assembling the most talent-dense team the logistics industry has ever seen Relay’s Mission is to free commerce from friction . Today, high delivery costs act as a hidden tax on e-commerce, quietly shaping what can be sold online and limiting who can participate. We envision a world where more goods move more freely between more people , making the online shopping experience seamless and accessible to everyone. THE TEAM • ~160 people , around half in engineering, product and data • 45+ advanced degrees across computer science, mathematics and operations research • Thousands of data points captured, calculated, analysed and predicted for every single parcel we handle • An intellectually vibrant culture of first‑principles thinking , tight feedback loops and relentless experimentation Relay delivers 400,000 parcels a day through people who don't work for us: van drivers who choose their own shifts, local shops that hold parcels, and couriers who take them to the door. We went from 3,000 parcels a day in London to 400,000 across the UK in under three years. Most delivery companies sell on price and volume, and find out later whether a client made them money. Sales teams are measured on what they sign, not on what a signing is worth. Relay wants every client, and every new shop in the network, to be one we'd choose again. That is harder for us than for most, because what a client is worth depends on how their parcels flow through a network that's still growing. Engineering and analytics engineering build what you design. Sales Highlights You own decision-making, not the model: you decide what a client or shop is worth and which signings sales should chase. The sales lead acts on your calls. What is a new client or a new shop worth, when its value depends on where it sits in a network that changes every month? What would you build so sales knows before it signs? Which signings become partners who do well with us, and what does that tell sales to look for? The quarter's target is set. What has to close by when for it to hold, and what would tell you early that it won't? A whole area, not a slice: you decide how sales values what it wins, and the result shows in what we sign next. Analytics at the front, not in support: the squad's roadmap follows the analysis, in a data team of about 30 across analytics, operational research and data science. The Opportunity As a Senior Pricing Analyst, B2B at Relay, you'll: Decide which Sales problems are real and which only look real, before anyone builds a fix. Design how Sales decides: which signals count, what a client or shop is worth, and what good looks like. Tell the sales lead what to change and what to stop, and get a decision. Build the thing that decides: data applications, monitors and alerts, not decks, using Claude and agents to ship your own tools. Go and look when the numbers and the street disagree: a new shop, a client's parcels at the sort centre. Get the missing data built, and prove whether each change worked. In a year, sales chooses what to go after on measures you built, and can see whether the quarter will land before it ends. We're looking for candidates who… Have owned B2B pricing or commercial decisions and their number, rather than maintaining sales dashboards. Have built, hands on, the first version of how a company values a customer or a deal: unit economics, lifetime value, or what it costs to win one. Have seen their work acted on: a leader changed a plan, a team adopted your method, or sales went after different deals because of it. You wait, until you can’t. Alan exists to end the wait. Health is a universal right, and we believe this right can only become real when it’s coupled with prevention. We need to stop treating health as something we repair and start treating it as something we build, every day. It’s not solely a question of willpower. It’s the healthcare system itself that needs to work for everyone, in a sustainable way. So we are building the new standard in prevention insurance. Alan is the first company that integrates insurance, prevention, and care into a single, acclaimed user experience. We are on an incredible journey to build a global leading company, with a unique culture . We already partner with 40K+ companies of all sizes, serving more than 1M+ members, and have reached €800M+ in ARR. Prevention as the new norm. That's what we're building with our team of 1000+ people. If it speaks to you: we're hiring across France, Spain, Belgium, and Canada. And beyond. ⚡ The design and research community at Alan Alan’s Design & Research (D&R) community is the group of designers and researchers behind everything our members see and use. Our goal is simple: build the most member-centric health experience there is, with high standards of craft and a real understanding of the people we design for. We are growing fast, and AI is changing what is possible in the way we work. We are looking for someone who loves tooling, ops and AI to help us move faster without lowering the bar on quality. This is a builder role where design, operations and AI meet. You will scope where AI and automation can help us build faster, scale better and catch quality issues earlier, then turn the best ideas into tools the community actually uses. Build : Create skills, agents and automated checks that make design and research work more efficient, reliable and of higher quality. jobs.description: À propos de Dastra Dastra est une plateforme SaaS dédiée à la protection des données, à la conformité et à la gouvernance de l'IA. Nous accompagnons des organisations de toutes tailles dans la structuration et le pilotage de leurs enjeux de conformité, avec une ambition : rendre des sujets complexes plus simples, accessibles et opérationnels. Piloter les Proof of Concept (POC) : définir les critères de succès, organiser les validations techniques et apporter les preuves concrètes de l'adéquation de notre solution aux besoins du client. Assurer la continuité entre avant-vente et déploiement : collaborer avec les équipes Sales, Produit, Customer Success et Professional Services pour cadrer les besoins et garantir une transmission technique structurée après signature. Tu contribueras également à l'amélioration continue de nos pratiques avant-vente, de nos démonstrations et de notre documentation technique. Tu as l'habitude d'accompagner des cycles de vente complexes auprès de grands comptes , avec des interlocuteurs métiers et techniques exigeants. Tu possèdes une solide compréhension des architectures SaaS, des intégrations, des problématiques de sécurité et des environnements IT. Tu connais les enjeux de Privacy, conformité, GRC ou cybersécurité , et sais les traduire en solutions concrètes pour tes clients. Tu combines expertise technique, sens commercial et excellente communication : tu sais vulgariser des sujets complexes, convaincre et adapter ton discours à tes interlocuteurs. Tu fais preuve d'agilité intellectuelle, de pédagogie, de pragmatisme et de sang-froid, y compris lors de démonstrations en direct. Un environnement stimulant : évoluer à l'intersection du SaaS, de la protection des données, de la cybersécurité et de l'intelligence artificielle. jobs.title: Research and Development Engineer in Artificial Intelligence - 12 months contract
jobs.description: Who we are ? Télécom Paris, part of the IMT (Institut Mines-Télécom) and a founding member of the Institut Polytechnique de Paris, is one of France's top 6 general engineering schools. The mainspring of Télécom Paris is to train, imagine and undertake to design digital models, technologies and solutions for a society and economy that respect people and their environment. Modern distributed systems are increasingly complex, with multiple interconnected components, services, and autonomous agents interacting in dynamic environments. Ensuring their cybersecurity requires analysing potential attacks, understanding the strategies available to attackers and defenders, and verifying that critical security properties are preserved. Formal verification provides rigorous methods for addressing these challenges, allowing engineers to reason about system behaviours and establish mathematical guarantees. However, applying these techniques to realistic systems remains challenging. Verification problems can involve large state spaces and complex strategic interactions, while constructing formal models and specifying security properties often requires specialised expertise. The VITAMIN-C (VerIficaTion of A MultI-ageNt system for Cybersecurity) project aims to address these challenges by combining formal verification with artificial intelligence. Building on VITAMIN, an existing modular model-checking platform for multi-agent systems, the project develops methods and tools for analysing cybersecurity properties in distributed and autonomous systems. Attackers and defenders are represented as agents with specific capabilities, objectives, and available actions. Their interactions are analysed using attack graphs, temporal and strategic logics, and model-checking techniques. The project also investigates how AI can improve the efficiency and accessibility of these verification processes. A central objective of VITAMIN-C is to integrate AI techniques into the verification workflow. On the computational side, AI models will be investigated to guide the exploration of large state spaces and prioritise promising verification strategies. By learning from previously verified models and their associated results, these components can help identify relevant search directions and reduce the computational effort required by verification algorithms. On the usability side, the project explores AI-assisted interfaces that support engineers in constructing formal models and specifying security properties. These interfaces may exploit natural-language processing and large language models to interpret engineering descriptions, suggest formal representations, and assist users throughout the verification process. In both cases, the correctness of verification results remains the responsibility of the underlying formal methods, which validate the outcomes produced or suggested by AI components. Within this context, the R&D engineer will contribute to the design, implementation, and evaluation of AI techniques for VITAMIN-C. The work will focus on developing AI components for verification guidance, investigating natural-language and LLM-based assistance for formal modelling, and integrating these capabilities into the existing platform. The engineer will also participate in the preparation of training and evaluation datasets, the development of experimental benchmarks, and the assessment of the proposed approaches in terms of effectiveness, computational efficiency, and reliability. The overall objective is to make formal verification more scalable and accessible while preserving the rigorous guarantees provided by the verification framework. Télécom Paris, part of the IMT (Institut Mines-Télécom) and a founding member of the Institut Polytechnique de Paris, is one of France's top 6 general engineering schools. The mainspring of Télécom Paris is to train, imagine and undertake to design digital models, technologies and solutions for a society and economy that respect people and their environment. Modern distributed systems are increasingly complex, with multiple interconnected components, services, and autonomous agents interacting in dynamic environments. Ensuring their cybersecurity requires analysing both potential attacks and the strategies that defenders can adopt in response. Attackers may exploit sequences of vulnerabilities to compromise a system, while defenders may react through countermeasures such as access restrictions, system reconfigurations, or Moving Target Defense mechanisms. Traditional cybersecurity analysis techniques often focus on identifying vulnerabilities and possible attack paths, with limited support for reasoning about the strategic interactions between attackers and defenders. The VITAMIN-C (VerIficaTion of A MultI-ageNt system for Cybersecurity) project aims to address these challenges through formal verification. Building on VITAMIN, an existing modular model-checking platform for multi-agent systems, the project develops methods and tools for modelling and verifying cybersecurity properties in distributed and autonomous systems. Attackers and defenders are represented as agents with specific capabilities, objectives, and available actions. Their interactions are analysed using attack graphs, temporal and strategic logics, and model-checking techniques. This approach allows the verification of security properties, such as the preservation of confidentiality and integrity, as well as the synthesis of defensive strategies against known attack scenarios. A central challenge of the project concerns the scalability of formal verification when applied to realistic cybersecurity scenarios. To address this issue, VITAMIN-C investigates symbolic and abstract model-checking techniques, together with a modular architecture supporting the integration of different verification engines. Within this context, the R&D engineer will contribute to the design, implementation, and evaluation of formal verification techniques for VITAMIN-C. The work will focus on formal modelling of cybersecurity scenarios, strategic model checking, development and optimisation of verification algorithms, and their integration into the existing platform. The engineer will also participate in experimental evaluations using cybersecurity benchmarks and industrial use cases, contributing to the development of a practical verification tool. jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer - OpenCRQ
jobs.description: 🌀 The Company Founded in 2022, Filigran is a global cybersecurity company on a mission to empower defense teams to be proactive through open-source solutions that uncover threats and drive action. Filigran stands out in the cybersecurity ecosystem through its open-source, AI-powered and threat-informed approach to Continuous Threat Exposure Management (CTEM). Our eXtended Threat Management (XTM) platform brings together threat intelligence, exposure validation and cyber risk reduction, enabling organizations to better understand their threat landscape and take action. At the heart of Filigran is our open-source approach. Our vision is to unite defenders into a global community to make security more open, resilient and collaborative. As Filigran continues to scale globally, we are building the organization, infrastructure and capabilities needed for our next stage of growth. How we scale matters just as much as how fast we scale: our CORE values: Cohesion, Openness, Responsibility and Equity shape how we work together, make decisions and build for the future. 🎯 The Role We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer who is curious about the modeling problem underneath cyber risk and wants to help shape a young product. You will join OpenCRQ as its fourth engineer and work across the data model, backend and product surface. Many foundations are still being defined, giving you meaningful influence beyond the features you directly own. You will shape these decisions with the squad and experienced engineering and product leaders across Filigran. We value constructive disagreement, clear reasoning and shared outcomes, and we expect everyone to ask for context, challenge assumptions and learn from one another. 🧩 The problem you would be working on Ask a CISO what a cyber risk could cost, and the answer often still begins with a color: red, amber or green, often produced by a spreadsheet disconnected from current evidence. OpenCRQ replaces that color with a financial estimate and a traceable chain of evidence: which threat actors are active, which assets they can reach, which controls have proven effective and what the remaining exposure could cost. Every step is computed from live data and must withstand a simple question from a board: “Where does that figure come from?” That is what makes this an engineering problem rather than a reporting one. OpenCRQ is Filigran’s cyber risk quantification product. It combines threat intelligence from OpenCTI, exposure and control validation from OpenAEV, and agentic workflows through XTM One. As these products become more connected, the squad will define what agents can ask of the risk model, which evidence they can use and how their answers remain safe and explainable. 🛠️ What you would work on End-to-end product ownership. Take product problems from early ideation and technical design through implementation, end-to-end testing and validation with users. You will have the autonomy to drive the work, while using the squad to challenge assumptions and improve the outcome. The quantification engine. Turn threat frequency, control effectiveness and asset value into probabilistic loss distributions. Build general-purpose quantitative models that can evolve as assumptions and available evidence change, without losing reproducibility or explainability. The correlation layer. Model complex relationships across OpenCRQ, OpenCTI, OpenAEV and customer systems. Map threat intelligence, including intrusion sets, techniques, campaigns and observations, to assets, vulnerabilities, exposures and control coverage. This includes adapting OpenCRQ to open standards and schemas such as STIX and OCSF, without coupling the product to a single representation. Reliable ingestion at scale. Process hundreds of thousands of findings per tenant through delta syncs, long-running backfills and feeds with imperfect timestamps. You will help design observable, recoverable pipelines while extending tenant isolation as the domain

jobs.title: Product Frontend Engineer
jobs.description: quinn is becoming the way people employ, across the globe, through one app. quinn is an app-based, managed payroll and employment-administration service. We run it for private households employing a cleaner, nanny, or caretaker, and for businesses that manage employment relationships at scale. The customer stays the legal employer: quinn registers the employment, runs payroll, and handles social insurance, taxes, and filings on their behalf, automated end to end. Where everyone else sells software, quinn sells the outcome. We don't sell payroll software. We run payroll. The purpose behind it is simple: Fair employment. For all. Correct and fair employment, made simple and accessible for any employer and any employee, in any market quinn enters. Where this is going Think about what Revolut did to banking. All of the complexity (the regulation, the clearing, the compliance) handled invisibly in the background, and one simple experience at the front. Nobody using Revolut thinks about what happens behind the screen when they open a new account, swap currencies or send money abroad. It just works, in a couple of taps. Nobody should have to think about it in order to employ someone either. That is what quinn is building, and it is further along than most people assume: a profitable core business, running today in Switzerland, Germany and the UK, expanding into new markets both by launching and by acquiring. By 2030 quinn intends to be the destination brand for fair employment across six countries and more, on one platform, with one experience. One platform means one frontend. One experience means it looks and behaves like quinn whether you are in Zurich or in London, a household or a company. In this strategy that is not a nice-to-have. It is the strategy. Which is why the surface matters more than anything else. Everything quinn does is designed to disappear. The interface is the only part the customer ever sees, and it is the whole proof that the complexity behind it is really handled. Why this role exists Today , quinn runs on several separate web apps: one per product and market, each with its own frontend, grown over the years as the company grew. Our backend engineers built them alongside everything else, plus an internal admin tool that grew the same way. They all work: thousands of employers run payroll through them every month. But nobody was ever tasked with owning the frontend development, so each one got built the way frontend is built by Backend Developers, seen as a hassle rather than the main aspect users interactive with. What comes next is one frontend that replaces all of them, built from scratch: one quinn app for employers, employees and our own support team, in the browser first, then in the App Store and Google Play from the same work. Alongside it, the frontend of Maestro, the internal tool that replaces the old admin for batch processes. The phone app is the surface that matters most, so everything is built for it from the first screen rather than adapted to it afterwards. That is the opening. How we work We are AI-native, and we mean it operationally rather than as a slogan. AI is how the work gets done here. It is why a small team ships like a large one, and it is a large part of how one person will be able to hold the standard we are describing. We expect you to be at the front of that. Not to have heard of the tools, to live in them, and to build your own leverage with them: scaffolding, visual regression checks, design-token pipelines, whatever takes manual work out of the way. And we expect the judgement that has to come with it. AI writes code that looks right and is subtly wrong: structure that doesn't scale, patterns that fall apart three screens later, components that work once and never again. You take the speed and throw away the rest. AI never lowers the bar here. It is the reason the bar can be this high. Tasks What you will own Everything on the screen: The frontend of the quinn app and the web

jobs.title: Account Executive
jobs.description: <h1><span style="font-size: 12pt;"><strong>Join Proton and build a better internet where privacy is the default</strong></span></h1> <p>At Proton, we believe that privacy is a fundamental human right and the cornerstone of democracy. Since our inception in 2014, founded by a team of scientists from CERN, we have dedicated ourselves to providing free and open-source technology to millions worldwide, ensuring access to privacy, security, and freedom online.</p> <p>Our journey began with Proton Mail, the largest secure email service globally, and has since expanded to include Proton VPN, Proton Calendar, Proton Drive, and Proton Pass. These tools empower individuals and organizations to take control of their personal data, break away from Big Tech’s invasive practices, and defeat censorship. Our work impacts hundreds of millions of lives, from activists on the front lines defending freedom to leaders in governments protecting sensitive information. In some cases, Proton’s services have even been instrumental in saving lives by enabling secure and private communications in high-risk situations.</p> <p>Proton today supports over 100 million user accounts with a growing team of over 500 people from over 50 different countries, from the world's top companies and universities. We value intelligence, learning potential, and ambition in our hiring process. Adaptability is key as we navigate uncharted territories and redefine how business is conducted online. We believe smaller teams of exceptional talent will always prevail over larger teams with lower talent density. jobs.description: Jouw Missie bij CCS Geen dag is hetzelfde in deze rol. Je kunt deels thuiswerken, deels op ons kantoor in Woerden en bij verschillende klanten in Nederland. Tijdelijk werken vanuit het buitenland kan ook dankzij onze workation-regeling (maximaal 30 dagen aaneengesloten per jaar). Bij ons draait het om klantgericht werken én werkplezier. Daarom is er volop ruimte voor ontspanning en plezier. Denk aan een levend tafelvoetbaltoernooi, pubquiz en een bier- & wijnproeverij. Ons actieve Fun-team zorgt elke maand weer voor iets leuks. En als je reislust nog niet is gestild met 25 vakantiedagen en een workation, dan kun je zelfs tot 20 extra verlofdagen bijkopen. Hiermee zorg je voor proactieve en transparante rapportage over het project aan de klant. Na de lunch: Je checkt nog een paar tickets qua voortgang op het planboard, waarbij je de samenhang met de planning checkt. Vervolgens ga je naar de werksessie met het CCS projectmanagement guild. Daarbij ben je in staat om de klantverwachtingen helder te analyseren, te managen en actief bij te sturen waar nodig; · Je beheerst de Nederlandse en Engelse taal uitstekend in woord en geschrift; · Jouw persoonlijkheid kenmerkt zich door: gestructureerd, motiverend, communicatief sterk, duidelijk, open, tikje eigenwijs, enthousiast, relativerend, creatief en pragmatisch; · Je haalt energie uit het opstellen en bewaken van planningen, analyseren van gegevens en opstellen van duidelijke, gestructureerde rapportages en presentaties; · Je hebt minimaal een afgeronde bachelor, bij voorkeur richting bedrijfskunde, bedrijfseconomie en/of informatica. jobs.title: Product Engineer, Shop
jobs.description: ABOUT INSIFY We sell a mix of insurance products to small businesses (SME's) in the Netherlands, Germany and France, and we are in the process of scaling into more markets.  Insurance infrastructure is brutal to get right. Every carrier has its own spec, every product its own underwriting rules, every country its own regulatory requirements. Most insurers throw people and process at that complexity - one-off integrations, workarounds on workarounds. We're building it differently: our insurance platform is where we consolidate that complexity, so that launching a new product or market becomes a configuration exercise rather than a rebuild. Insify is a high-growth scale-up backed by more than €40M from investors like Accel, Munich Re Ventures, and Formula 1 champion Nico Rosberg. In five years we've expanded from the Netherlands into France and Germany. Our mission: become the European leader in AI-powered SME insurance. About the role You would join the Shop team, responsible for everything that happens after a small business buys a policy from us. You would help shape how the platform handles the next product and the next country, on a system already carrying live policies and real customers. The team owns end-to-end policy lifecycle management (mid-term adjustments, automated renewals, cancellations, and payment flows) alongside the backoffice tooling that gives our operations and support teams full visibility and control. We work closely with the Claims Team, and with the Activation Teams that turn a lead into a paying customer. Product and engineering together are 30+ people. Every country has its own regulatory quirks, and every insurance product has unique data structures, lifecycle rules, and money flows. As we expand across Europe, our goal isn't to write custom glue code for every new launch. It's to design elegant, reusable platform abstractions. We're building a system where introducing a new country or product feels like snapping modular building blocks together. You're joining at an exciting inflection point: we have real traction, proven scale, and you get to directly build the foundational platform that powers our next wave of European growth. What you'll be doing Owning end-to-end the discovery and delivery of crucial platform features that enable our ability to scale as an insurance business Continuously and relentlessly seeking opportunities to turn new product demands into platform capabilities and features that scale across countries and insurance product lines Challenging our ideas and bringing your own. We encourage each other to act this way, so you can expect the same from others What you'll need 3+ years building complex web applications and services, with real production ownership Ownership & impact instinct - when needed you go beyond your direct stack to get to results, be that data / backend / frontend You get real leverage out of AI in your daily work, and you can say where it helped, and where it hurt Strong fundamentals in domain-driven design & service oriented architecture Not all of the above are hard requirements. If you're strong on most of these and eager to grow into the rest, we'd still love to hear from you. Nice to have Experience building B2B products, especially in insurance & fintech Experience working on a product distributed across different country markets Strong observability instincts. You know where things will break, and can help others learn that too Our stack TypeScript across the board, running on AWS (IaaC), in a single monorepo. jobs.description: Company Overview Deepgram is the leading platform underpinning the emerging trillion-dollar Voice AI economy, providing real-time APIs for speech-to-text (STT), text-to-speech (TTS), and building production-grade voice agents at scale. More than 200,000 developers and 1,300+ organizations build voice offerings that are ‘Powered by Deepgram’, including Twilio, Cloudflare, Sierra, Decagon, Vapi, Daily, Cresta, Granola, and Jack in the Box. Deepgram’s voice-native foundation models are accessed through cloud APIs or as self-hosted and on-premises software, with unmatched accuracy, low latency, and cost efficiency. Backed by a recent Series C led by leading global investors and strategic partners, Deepgram has processed over 50,000 years of audio and transcribed more than 1 trillion words. There is no organization in the world that understands voice better than Deepgram. Company Operating Rhythm At Deepgram, we expect an AI-first mindset—AI use and comfort aren’t optional, they’re core to how we operate, innovate, and measure performance. Every team member who works at Deepgram is expected to actively use and experiment with advanced AI tools, and even build your own into your everyday work. We measure how effectively AI is applied to deliver results, and consistent, creative use of the latest AI capabilities is key to success here. Candidates should be comfortable adopting new models and modes quickly, integrating AI into their workflows, and continuously pushing the boundaries of what these technologies can do. Additionally, we move at the pace of AI. Change is rapid, and you can expect your day-to-day work to evolve just as quickly. This may not be the right role if you’re not excited to experiment, adapt, think on your feet, and learn constantly, or if you’re seeking something highly prescriptive with a traditional 9-to-5. The Opportunity Voice is the most natural modality for human interaction with machines. However, current sequence modeling paradigms based on jointly scaling model and data cannot deliver voice AI capable of universal human interaction. The challenges are rooted in fundamental data problems posed by audio: real-world audio data is scarce and enormously diverse, spanning a vast space of voices, speaking styles, and acoustic conditions. Even if billions of hours of audio were accessible, its inherent high dimensionality creates computational and storage costs that make training and deployment prohibitively expensive at world scale. We believe that entirely new paradigms for audio AI are needed to overcome these challenges and make voice interaction accessible to everyone. The Role As a Member of the Research Staff, you will pioneer the development of Latent Space Models (LSMs), a new approach that aims to solve the fundamental data, scale, and cost challenges associated with building robust, contextualized voice AI. Your research will focus on solving one or more of the following problems: Build next-generation neural audio codecs that achieve extreme, low bit-rate compression and high fidelity reconstruction across a world-scale corpus of general audio. Pioneer steerable generative models that can synthesize the full diversity of human speech from the codec latent representation, from casual conversation to highly emotional expression to complex multi-speaker scenarios with environmental noise and overlapping speech. Develop embedding systems that cleanly factorize the codec latent space into interpretable dimensions of speaker, content, style, environment, and channel effects -- enabling precise control over each aspect and the ability to massively amplify an existing seed dataset through “latent recombination”. Leverage latent recombination to generate synthetic audio data at previously impossible scales, unlocking joint model and data scaling paradigms for audio. Endeavor to train multimodal speech-to-speech systems that can 1) understand any human irrespective of their demographics, state, or environment

jobs.title: Forward Deployed Engineer (f/m/d)
jobs.description: About Valova We are building the AI operations platform for European hospitals, so every clinician can focus on patients. Behind every patient sits a chain of admin work: documentation, coding, billing, audits, scheduling. It runs through disconnected systems and endless manual hand-offs , while most German hospitals already operate at a loss . We start where the impact is measurable from day one: case to cash . Valova codes every case, defends it in audits and makes sure the money lands. From there we take on every workflow that runs a hospital , until one agentic system handles the routine and people decide the exceptions. First Germany, then Europe. Doctors, engineers and operators, on-site in Munich and Berlin . Join us! Why this role matters Valova only works as well as it fits into the hospital. Our product creates the most value when it’s deeply connected to a hospital’s systems and built around how coders and medical controlling actually work. Today, connecting to a hospital information system can take months. That’s time hospitals keep losing revenue and coders keep working by hand. That’s where you come in. As Forward Deployed Engineer, you own technical go-lives from start to finish : from the first sandbox to production, from the interface to the workflow on the ward. You’re the bridge between hospital IT, the people who use Valova and our engineering team . Your impact is easy to see: in hospitals that go live faster, in integrations that run reliably, and in a product that gets better with every deployment because you bring back what you learn. This is a hands-on engineering role with real code in production and direct influence on our roadmap. It’s not a support desk, not a pre-sales role and not project management where others do the building. And it’s not a desk job: you’ll regularly be on site in hospitals How the role sits in the team You report directly to Christian, our CTO, and work day to day with our engineering team on connectors, deployments and internal tooling. With Malte and our product team, you turn what you see in hospitals into clear requirements. In hospital projects, you work hand in hand with our customer success and sales team and on the hospital side with IT leads, KIS vendors, coders and medical controlling. What you will do Bring hospitals live: You take hospitals from sandbox to production, deploy Valova on hospital VMs and connect it to KIS systems such as SAP i.s.h.med, Orbis or Dedalus. Build the connections: You build and maintain interfaces (HL7, FHIR, archive and document exports) together with hospital IT and their partners. Set up Valova for each customer: You configure document types, case filtering, department rules and coding workflows. Learn from the ward: You work on site with coders and medical controlling and turn their friction into clear product requirements. Make deployments repeatable: You write the code that makes the next go-live faster: connectors, scripts, monitoring and internal tooling. Earn the hospital’s trust: You answer technical questions in security and data protection reviews (BSI C5, GDPR). What we are looking for: Engineering experience: At least two years in software engineering, and you’re comfortable with Linux, Docker and basic networking. Integration know-how: You’ve worked on system integrations. Experience with HL7/FHIR or SAP environments is a big plus. Customer focus: You enjoy working with customers and explain technical topics clearly to IT leads and coders alike. High ownership: You move things forward, even when three parties are involved. Travel: You’re happy to spend around 30 percent of your time at hospitals across Germany. Languages: You speak fluent German and English, since our customers work in German. Location: You work from our office in Munich or Berlin. Missing one or two points, but convinced you’re the right person for this role? Apply anyway. We’re looking forward to meeting you! jobs.description: Seit über 25 Jahren verwandeln wir bei der Windhoff Group Daten in echte Geschäftschancen – von klassischer Business Intelligence bis zur KI-getriebenen Automatisierung. Getragen wird unser Wachstum von unserem Gesellschafter Aurelius, einem globalen Private-Equity-Investor, der seit 2023 an der Windhoff Group beteiligt ist. Unser SAP-Kerngeschäft bauen wir dabei gezielt zu einer Multi-Vendor-Strategie aus – mit Databricks, Snowflake, Dremio sowie den Cloud-Plattformen Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud und AWS (u. a. Amazon Athena). Du profitierst von einem Marktumfeld, das deutlich stärker wächst als der klassische IT-Dienstleistungsmarkt – und von einem Unternehmen, das dieses Wachstum aktiv mitgestaltet, statt nur zu verwalten. Neben unserer fachlichen Expertise sind wir ein Arbeitgeber, der Vielfalt fördert und sicherstellt, dass alle Mitarbeitenden fair behandelt werden. Teile uns mit, wenn wir auf etwas besonders Rücksicht nehmen sollen - wie zum Beispiel auf bestimmte Arbeitszeiten oder andere Rahmenbedingungen, deine Situation im Privatleben oder besondere Bedürfnisse bei der Arbeit. Du konzipierst und implementierst Datenmodelle sowie ETL-/ELT-Strecken, häufig in hybriden Szenarien, in denen SAP mit Databricks, Snowflake, Dremio und den gängigen Cloud-Plattformen zusammenspielt. Je nach Karrierestufe übernimmst du die Verantwortung für Teilprojekte oder ganze Projekte und für das Windhoff Projektteam. Als Lead Consultant entwickelst du außerdem deine KollegInnen fachlich weiter. Du baust unseren Databricks-Fachbereich mit auf und gestaltest unsere Multi-Vendor-Strategie mit SAP als Kern aktiv mit. Qualifikation Du hast relevante Berufserfahrung im SAP Data Engineering oder mit Databricks, zum Beispiel als SAP Data Engineer, SAP BW Consultant, SAP Datasphere Consultant oder Data Engineer. Du kennst dich mit SAP Datasphere und dem Databricks Lakehouse aus, beherrschst SQL-Script und Python sicher und hast ETL-/ELT-Prozesse bereits erfolgreich umgesetzt. The simplest system that reliably solves the real problem wins. What you'll bring Strong Python and backend engineering. You think beyond individual services or screens: how data, algorithms, product, and infrastructure fit together. Infrastructure fundamentals. You are comfortable with Docker, CI/CD, deployment, observability, and operating services. Independence. jobs.title: Product Manager - Snacks
jobs.description: Vilgain makes high-quality food - clean, functional ingredients, no shortcuts, no filler additives . We're 700+ people across Prague, Brno and London, already selling in 12+ markets across Europe, the UK, the US and beyond. We're on a mission to change how people think about food , and we're growing fast to do it - expanding internationally and building a company where people have a real say in what we make and how we make it, not just a seat at the table. Your mission 🎯 You'll own specific product development projects from brief to launch, working directly with third-party suppliers and manufacturers. Working closely with the Category Manager, you'll make sure every project is aligned with the wider category goals and launch plan, and spot the commercial opportunities that will help the category grow. What will you do? Owning end-to-end new product development projects, from initial brief through development to market launch. Running projects with third-party manufacturers – sourcing and selecting suppliers and managing those relationships day to day. Reporting into the Category Manager and making sure your projects are aligned with the wider category goals and launch plan. Building the commercial case for your projects – costings, margins and volumes – and prioritising the opportunities with the highest value. Partnering with design, marketing, Regulatory and QA to bring products to market, including briefs, documentation and artwork sign-off. Running existing product development (EPD) projects such as product improvements, packaging amends and label corrections. Monitoring market trends and identifying new commercial opportunities for the category. What do we expect from you? At least 3 years' experience in NPD, project management or a similar role in the food industry – food experience is essential. Experience with private label production and working with third-party manufacturers. Highly numerate and financially aware, with the commercial sense to prioritise high-value opportunities. Experience in a small business or startup environment – we move quickly, and you'll need to be happy with the fast pace of a rapidly growing business. Highly organised, with strong attention to detail and the ability to juggle several projects at once. A proactive problem-solver who takes initiative and can work independently. A strong communicator who can build good relationships with colleagues, both internally and externally. Confident with spreadsheets and project management tools, and actively uses AI tools to work smarter. A love for food and a genuine interest in making a difference to the food system. Fluent in English. What we offer: Based in London, hybrid – minimum 3 days a week in the office. Fast-paced, growing team where your work has a visible impact on the products we launch. 5 weeks of vacation, flexible hours, and remote work options, get monthly shopping credits. Stay connected through team events, breakfasts, and group workouts. Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

jobs.title: Senior Pricing Analyst, B2B
jobs.description: Relay is fundamentally reshaping how goods move in an online era. Backed by Europe’s largest-ever logistics Series A ($35M) led by deep-tech investors Plural, and a recently closed Series B ($95M), Relay is scaling faster than 99% of venture-backed startups. We're assembling the most talent-dense team the logistics industry has ever seen Relay’s Mission is to free commerce from friction . Today, high delivery costs act as a hidden tax on e-commerce, quietly shaping what can be sold online and limiting who can participate. We envision a world where more goods move more freely between more people , making the online shopping experience seamless and accessible to everyone. THE TEAM • ~160 people , around half in engineering, product and data • 45+ advanced degrees across computer science, mathematics and operations research • Thousands of data points captured, calculated, analysed and predicted for every single parcel we handle • An intellectually vibrant culture of first‑principles thinking , tight feedback loops and relentless experimentation Relay delivers 400,000 parcels a day through people who don't work for us: van drivers who choose their own shifts, local shops that hold parcels, and couriers who take them to the door. We went from 3,000 parcels a day in London to 400,000 across the UK in under three years. Most delivery companies sell on price and volume, and find out later whether a client made them money. Sales teams are measured on what they sign, not on what a signing is worth. Relay wants every client, and every new shop in the network, to be one we'd choose again. That is harder for us than for most, because what a client is worth depends on how their parcels flow through a network that's still growing. Engineering and analytics engineering build what you design. Sales Highlights You own decision-making, not the model: you decide what a client or shop is worth and which signings sales should chase. The sales lead acts on your calls. What is a new client or a new shop worth, when its value depends on where it sits in a network that changes every month? What would you build so sales knows before it signs? Which signings become partners who do well with us, and what does that tell sales to look for? The quarter's target is set. What has to close by when for it to hold, and what would tell you early that it won't? A whole area, not a slice: you decide how sales values what it wins, and the result shows in what we sign next. Analytics at the front, not in support: the squad's roadmap follows the analysis, in a data team of about 30 across analytics, operational research and data science. The Opportunity As a Senior Pricing Analyst, B2B at Relay, you'll: Decide which Sales problems are real and which only look real, before anyone builds a fix. Design how Sales decides: which signals count, what a client or shop is worth, and what good looks like. Tell the sales lead what to change and what to stop, and get a decision. Build the thing that decides: data applications, monitors and alerts, not decks, using Claude and agents to ship your own tools. Go and look when the numbers and the street disagree: a new shop, a client's parcels at the sort centre. Get the missing data built, and prove whether each change worked. In a year, sales chooses what to go after on measures you built, and can see whether the quarter will land before it ends. We're looking for candidates who… Have owned B2B pricing or commercial decisions and their number, rather than maintaining sales dashboards. Have built, hands on, the first version of how a company values a customer or a deal: unit economics, lifetime value, or what it costs to win one. Have seen their work acted on: a leader changed a plan, a team adopted your method, or sales went after different deals because of it. Today, high delivery costs act as a hidden tax on e-commerce, quietly shaping what can be sold online and limiting who can participate. THE TEAM • ~160 people , around half in engineering, product and data • 45+ advanced degrees across computer science, mathematics and operations research • Thousands of data points captured, calculated, analysed and predicted for every single parcel we handle • An intellectually vibrant culture of first‑principles thinking , tight feedback loops and relentless experimentation Every courier who works with Relay chooses their day. A day is a set of routes that have to fit together, and every courier's ideal day competes with everyone else's. Work is finite and every route still has to be covered, so matching thousands of couriers to the work they want is a recommendation problem with few precedents. Science at Relay is the brain of the operation: machine learning, operational research, recommender systems, causal inference, location intelligence and experimentation, working together to decide how every parcel gets delivered. There's no existing recommender to iterate on. You'll build it. Recommender Systems Highlights Combinatorial, constrained and competitive: every recommendation has to be feasible for the whole network, not just right for one courier. Télécom Paris, part of the IMT (Institut Mines-Télécom) and a founding member of the Institut Polytechnique de Paris, is one of France's top 6 general engineering schools. The mainspring of Télécom Paris is to train, imagine and undertake to design digital models, technologies and solutions for a society and economy that respect people and their environment. Modern distributed systems are increasingly complex, with multiple interconnected components, services, and autonomous agents interacting in dynamic environments. Ensuring their cybersecurity requires analysing potential attacks, understanding the strategies available to attackers and defenders, and verifying that critical security properties are preserved. Formal verification provides rigorous methods for addressing these challenges, allowing engineers to reason about system behaviours and establish mathematical guarantees. However, applying these techniques to realistic systems remains challenging. Verification problems can involve large state spaces and complex strategic interactions, while constructing formal models and specifying security properties often requires specialised expertise. The VITAMIN-C (VerIficaTion of A MultI-ageNt system for Cybersecurity) project aims to address these challenges by combining formal verification with artificial intelligence. Building on VITAMIN, an existing modular model-checking platform for multi-agent systems, the project develops methods and tools for analysing cybersecurity properties in distributed and autonomous systems. Attackers and defenders are represented as agents with specific capabilities, objectives, and available actions. Their interactions are analysed using attack graphs, temporal and strategic logics, and model-checking techniques. The project also investigates how AI can improve the efficiency and accessibility of these verification processes. A central objective of VITAMIN-C is to integrate AI techniques into the verification workflow. On the computational side, AI models will be investigated to guide the exploration of large state spaces and prioritise promising verification strategies. By learning from previously verified models and their associated results, these components can help identify relevant search directions and reduce the computational effort required by verification algorithms. On the usability side, the project explores AI-assisted interfaces that support engineers in constructing formal models and specifying security properties. These interfaces may exploit natural-language processing and large language models to interpret engineering descriptions, suggest formal representations, and assist users throughout the verification process. In both cases, the correctness of verification results remains the responsibility of the underlying formal methods, which validate the outcomes produced or suggested by AI components. Within this context, the R&D engineer will contribute to the design, implementation, and evaluation of AI techniques for VITAMIN-C. The work will focus on developing AI components for verification guidance, investigating natural-language and LLM-based assistance for formal modelling, and integrating these capabilities into the existing platform. The overall objective is to make formal verification more scalable and accessible while preserving the rigorous guarantees provided by the verification framework. jobs.description: 🌀 The Company Founded in 2022, Filigran is a global cybersecurity company on a mission to empower defense teams to be proactive through open-source solutions that uncover threats and drive action. Filigran stands out in the cybersecurity ecosystem through its open-source, AI-powered and threat-informed approach to Continuous Threat Exposure Management (CTEM). Our eXtended Threat Management (XTM) platform brings together threat intelligence, exposure validation and cyber risk reduction, enabling organizations to better understand their threat landscape and take action. At the heart of Filigran is our open-source approach. Our vision is to unite defenders into a global community to make security more open, resilient and collaborative. As Filigran continues to scale globally, we are building the organization, infrastructure and capabilities needed for our next stage of growth. How we scale matters just as much as how fast we scale: our CORE values: Cohesion, Openness, Responsibility and Equity shape how we work together, make decisions and build for the future. 🎯 The Role We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer who is curious about the modeling problem underneath cyber risk and wants to help shape a young product. You will join OpenCRQ as its fourth engineer and work across the data model, backend and product surface. Many foundations are still being defined, giving you meaningful influence beyond the features you directly own. You will shape these decisions with the squad and experienced engineering and product leaders across Filigran. We value constructive disagreement, clear reasoning and shared outcomes, and we expect everyone to ask for context, challenge assumptions and learn from one another. 🧩 The problem you would be working on Ask a CISO what a cyber risk could cost, and the answer often still begins with a color: red, amber or green, often produced by a spreadsheet disconnected from current evidence. OpenCRQ replaces that color with a financial estimate and a traceable chain of evidence: which threat actors are active, which assets they can reach, which controls have proven effective and what the remaining exposure could cost. Every step is computed from live data and must withstand a simple question from a board: “Where does that figure come from?” That is what makes this an engineering problem rather than a reporting one. OpenCRQ is Filigran’s cyber risk quantification product. It combines threat intelligence from OpenCTI, exposure and control validation from OpenAEV, and agentic workflows through XTM One. As these products become more connected, the squad will define what agents can ask of the risk model, which evidence they can use and how their answers remain safe and explainable. 🛠️ What you would work on End-to-end product ownership. Take product problems from early ideation and technical design through implementation, end-to-end testing and validation with users. You will have the autonomy to drive the work, while using the squad to challenge assumptions and improve the outcome. The quantification engine. Turn threat frequency, control effectiveness and asset value into probabilistic loss distributions. Build general-purpose quantitative models that can evolve as assumptions and available evidence change, without losing reproducibility or explainability. The correlation layer. Model complex relationships across OpenCRQ, OpenCTI, OpenAEV and customer systems. Map threat intelligence, including intrusion sets, techniques, campaigns and observations, to assets, vulnerabilities, exposures and control coverage. This includes adapting OpenCRQ to open standards and schemas such as STIX and OCSF, without coupling the product to a single representation. Reliable ingestion at scale. Process hundreds of thousands of findings per tenant through delta syncs, long-running backfills and feeds with imperfect timestamps. You will help design observable, recoverable pipelines while extending tenant isolation as the domain

jobs.description: At Brevo, we’re not just building a CRM. With our technology, we’re helping millions of organizations build lasting relationships with their customers. You move fluidly between a system design discussion, a code review, a production incident, a migration plan, and an executive-level technical decision. You bring deep expertise in several of the following: Kubernetes, CI/CD, Kafka, ClickHouse, OpenTelemetry, distributed databases, service communication, developer platforms, and large-scale observability. Loft's AI for Space group is building the stack that runs real machine learning in orbit; turning raw sensor data into decisions on the satellite itself, so insight reaches the customer in minutes instead of hours. The AI Engineering team is where models meet the spacecraft. We own the full path from a partner's trained model to something that actually runs — fast — on flight hardware: compiling ONNX models into optimized engines for each accelerator, the Space Inference Engine and its execution providers, the SDK that packages models for flight, and the perf tooling that proves a model fits its power, thermal, and latency budget before it ever leaves the ground. As our ML Runtime Engineer , you'll own model compilation and the performance tooling behind it. jobs.description: Mindset Chez Thiga, nous considérons qu’un Design System n’est pas seulement un ensemble de composants ou de règles : c’est un produit à part entière . Un produit pensé pour évoluer, répondre aux besoins des équipes, et accompagner la croissance de l’entreprise. Créer et faire vivre un Design System demande une vision , une stratégie claire , et une gouvernance solide . Il faut piloter son adoption, anticiper ses usages à grande échelle, et s’assurer qu’il réponde aux enjeux à la fois du Design et de la Tech. C’est un levier puissant pour faire monter en maturité les organisations, structurer la collaboration entre les équipes, et diffuser une culture produit forte. Aujourd'hui, un Design System bien structuré est aussi la condition sine qua non pour tirer pleinement parti de l'IA dans les workflows design et prototypage. Tokens cohérents, composants documentés, nomenclature rigoureuse autant de fondations qui permettent d'exploiter les outils d'IA générative (Figma Make, Lovable, v0...) de manière fiable et scalable. Le.la Design System Manager de demain est celui.celle qui anticipe ces usages et structure son système en conséquence. Les Design System Managers que nous recherchons pensent leur système comme un produit vivant, automatisé au maximum, et conçu pour connecter Design et Ingénierie dans un workflow sans friction . How we work together 🤝 Mettre en place des rituels d'adoption et d'amélioration continue :offices hours, sessions de feedback, contribution guidelines pour que le DS soit co-construit et adopté par toutes les équipes. Aligner Design et Engineering en continu : organiser des syncs réguliers avec les équipes dev pour garantir la cohérence entre les composants Figma et leur implémentation code. Le DS ne vit pas dans Figma seul; il vit dans la production. Piloter l'alignement stratégique multi-équipes : s'assurer que Produit, Tech, Design et business partagent la même vision et roadmap du DS, intégrée au même niveau que les autres produits. Répondre aux besoins des utilisateurs et contributeurs : centraliser les demandes, prioriser les évolutions, et faciliter la contribution fluide de designers, développeurs et PMs. Fédérer autour d'une culture DS partagée : faire du DS un produit vivant et co-créé, en favorisant des échanges transparents et en embarquant les équipes dans sa vision long terme How we get work done 🚀 Définir et piloter la roadmap du DS : feuille de route alignée sur les priorités produit et business, avec des objectifs mesurables à court et long terme. Automatiser les workflows du DS au maximum : pipelines de tokens, synchronisation design to code en temps réel, scripts de génération de documentation, réduire au minimum les tâches manuelles et les risques de désynchronisation. Structurer le DS pour l'IA et le prototypage rapide : concevoir une architecture de composants et de tokens qui rende le DS exploitable par les outils d'IA générative (Figma Make, Cursor, v0, Lovable...). Cela implique : nomenclature stricte,variantes bien définies, props documentées, et une logique de composants qui s'aligne avec les patterns du code. Garantir la cohérence design-code : mettre en place des outils de vérification automatique pour s'assurer que ce qui est designé est bien ce qui est développé sans avoir à le vérifier manuellement. Promouvoir les bonnes pratiques à grande échelle : formations, ateliers, documentation vivante pour que le DS soit utilisé de manière fluide et scalable par toutes les équipes.
